source_text:
De partibus animae
Τῆς δὲ ψυχῆς μέρη γʹ. Ἐπιθυμητικὸν, θυμικὸν, λογιστικόν. Ἀρεταῖς δὲ τέσσαρσι
τεθρόνισται ὁ ἱερώτατος νοῦς· φρονήσεως, ἀνδρείας, δικαιοσύνης, σωφροσύνης.
95.232 Τρισσὸς ὁ νόμος. Φυσικὸς, γραπτὸς, καὶ ὁ ἐν χάριτι πνευματικός. Τετραμερές
ἐστι τὸ σῶμα, ὥσπερ τις κόσμος συνιστάμενον· τριμερὴς δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ ἡ ψυχὴ, προτυποῦσα
τὴν ἁγίαν Τριάδα, καὶ τοῦτο ταῖς ἐνεργείαις ζωοποιοῦσα. Τριμερῆ δὲ λέγομεν τὴν
ψυχὴν, ἔχουσαν λογικὸν, θυμικὸν, καὶ ἐπιθυμητικόν· ἵνα διὰ μὲν τοῦ λογικοῦ
λογίζηται· διὰ δὲ τοῦ θυμικοῦ ὀργίζηται τοῖς δαίμοσιν, ἀνδριζομένη κατ' αὐτῶν· διὰ δὲ
τοῦ ἐπιθυμητικοῦ ἀγαπᾷ τὸν Θεόν.
thought_title: The soul's three parts and the four virtues
orientation: The treatise opens by listing the parts of the soul and the virtues on which the intellect is enthroned, then describes the threefold law and the body-soul relationship.
pass_a_gloss: Of the soul the parts are three. Appetitive part, spirited part, rational part. On four virtues is enthroned the most sacred intellect: of understanding, of courage, of justice, of temperance. Threefold is the law. Natural, written, and the one in grace spiritual. Four-parted is the body, like some cosmos being composed; but tripartite in it is the soul, prefiguring the Holy Trinity, and this by its activities giving life. But tripartite we say the soul is, having rational part, spirited part, and appetitive part; so that through the rational part it may reason; through the spirited part it may be angry with the demons, acting courageously against them; through the appetitive part it may love God.

choices.why: Glossary English for the desiring part of the soul; avoids banned 'desire'.
Glossary English for the irascible part; avoids banned 'irascible part' and 'temper'.
Glossary English for the reasoning part; avoids banned 'reason' and 'reasoning part'.
Glossary English for the mind; avoids banned 'mind'.
Renders the middle participle as an active courageous stance against demons, matching the spirited part's function.
Literal rendering of the participle; the soul gives life to the body through its activities.

pass_b_english: The soul has three parts: the appetitive part, the spirited part, and the rational part. The most sacred intellect is enthroned on four virtues: understanding, courage, justice, and temperance.

The law is threefold: natural, written, and spiritual in grace. The body is fourfold, composed like a cosmos, while the soul within it is tripartite, prefiguring the Holy Trinity and giving life to the body through its activities. We say the soul is tripartite because it has a rational part, a spirited part, and an appetitive part. Through the rational part it thinks; through the spirited part it is angry with demons, acting courageously against them; and through the appetitive part it loves God.
